$comment: PER-CONTEXT CONSTRAINTS — the guidance that arrives WITH the scope.
THE GAP THIS CLOSES. .claude/CLAUDE.md is canonical and it is good, but it is
written for the repository as a whole, while context-map.json splits the code
into 143 contexts across 17 groups. The two meet only at the top: an agent
handed one context (10-22 files) gets the GLOBAL document and has to infer
which of its rules bind the files in front of it. Most of them do not. The
`db.transaction()` rules are irrelevant to a design-system context and the
dual-theme rules are irrelevant to a store module, and an agent that cannot
tell which is which either re-reads everything or guesses.
This file is the missing rung: a constraint record a loader can ATTACH to a
scope. Given a file path (or a context's `file_paths` from context-map.json),
resolve every zone whose `paths` match and prepend its `constraints` to the
agent's context. Zones are ordered general -> specific and a file may match
several: app/features/hiring/pipeline/PipelineTab.tsx matches `ui-surfaces`
and `i18n-catalogs`, and all of it applies.
WHY PATH GLOBS AND NOT CONTEXT IDS. context-map.json's per-context
`file_paths` are a generated snapshot (2026-08-21, regenerated by a rescan
that had already moved 285 contexts to 143). Keying constraints to that list
would make this file go stale on a rename rather than on a change of rule.
Paths are the stable axis, they are what the map's own contexts are built
from, and they are what a loader actually holds when an agent opens a file.
WRITTEN vs ASSUMED — the distinction this file exists to make readable.
`status` is the whole point. `written` means someone stated the constraint
and named what enforces it. A path in this tree matched by NO zone has
`assumed` guidance: the global document is all there is for it, which may be
correct and is at least now VISIBLE rather than indistinguishable from a rule
nobody wrote down. `coverage` below records what is deliberately not covered.
`enforced_by` IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD. It separates a constraint a gate
will catch from one that only a reviewer will. `prose` means exactly that:
nothing runs, so breaking it costs a review round and not a red build. Do not
write `enforced_by` for a gate you have not confirmed runs — an invented
enforcer is worse than an honest `prose`, because it tells the next agent it
is safe to stop thinking.

zones.title: better-sqlite3 stores — the rules that lose data silently

constraints.rule: Never `await` inside a `db.transaction()` callback.
constraints.why: better-sqlite3 transactions are synchronous. An await yields the event loop between BEGIN and COMMIT and the atomicity is gone with no error and no failing test — the code looks transactional and is not. Do the slow work (LLM call, subprocess, fetch) outside and bridge with a compare-and-swap on the row you read.

constraints.rule: A read -> compute -> write either takes the write lock or re-checks.
constraints.why: The two valid strategies are `db.transaction(...).immediate()` (lock at BEGIN) or a compensating precondition in the UPDATE's WHERE plus a `res.changes === 0` skip. A plain `tx()` whose UPDATE does not re-assert the status its SELECT filtered on is a lost update. `actOnPipelineEntry` is the canonical right shape; `closeEntriesByJobId` / `reopenEntriesByJobId` are the wrong and right shapes of one operation.

constraints.rule: A one-shot seeder records that it ran in `seed_marks`, never `COUNT(*) > 0`.
constraints.why: A row count cannot tell 'never seeded' from 'seeded, then legitimately emptied', and the difference is demo data reappearing in a real install.

constraints.rule: ANY new persistent table is workspace-scoped and listed in the tenancy manifest.
constraints.why: app/_lib/tenancy.ts is fail-closed: it allowlists verified workspace-scoped tables (each proven by a colocated *-tenancy.test.ts) and genuinely-global exempt tables. A new table is a reported gap until scoped and listed. Do not clear the gap by adding it to the exempt list without the reasoning.

constraints.rule: Do not re-export from the `app/_lib/db` barrel in a hub module.
constraints.why: `app/_lib/db.ts` is an `export *` over 17 stores and next compiles a route's whole module graph, so one value import taxes every route downstream. Import the slice.

zones.title: Route handlers — the money, the subprocesses and the auth edge

constraints.rule: A route is public only if it is on the allow-list, and sensitive routes re-verify anyway.
constraints.why: app/_lib/auth/public-routes.ts is the allow-list; sensitive handlers call requireOperator as defense in depth rather than trusting the middleware alone.
constraints.enforced_by: prose + route auth tests (npm run test:unit)

constraints.rule: Every open route that spends money or spawns a subprocess calls `rateLimit()`.
constraints.why: Per-IP / per-token limiting is the only thing between a public tokenized surface and an LLM bill or a fork bomb of python processes.
constraints.enforced_by: app/api/rate-limit-contract.test.ts — it pins which routes call rateLimit() and how, so adding, moving or re-keying a limiter means updating the contract deliberately, not deleting the assertion

constraints.rule: `maxDuration` is serverless-only — it does not bound a self-hosted handler.
constraints.why: Self-hosted `next start` does not kill long handlers. The real bound is a route-level timeout (e.g. the extract-text child-process timeout); do not rely on the platform.

constraints.rule: Do not import another route handler.
constraints.why: A route is an HTTP entry point, not a module — importing one runs its side effects in your graph. Share the lib function the handler calls.

zones.title: Candidate-facing tokenized pages — capability links, never sessions

constraints.rule: The response carries an explicit field allowlist — a projection, never the store row.
constraints.why: These surfaces are reached by a capability token held by someone who has no account. Serializing a row puts internal ids, other candidates' identifiers and unshipped fields on a public wire. `publicInviteView` in app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts is the shape to copy.
constraints.enforced_by: prose + per-route projection tests (npm run test:unit)

constraints.rule: A token is a capability, not a session. Never mint or read an operator session here.
constraints.why: The whole point of the tokenized surface is that the candidate is not a user of the workspace.

constraints.rule: These pages are localized and are held at ERROR for hardcoded strings.
constraints.why: They are the most-seen surfaces in a four-language product and the ones a recruiter never previews.
constraints.enforced_by: eslint i18next/no-literal-string (error on these globs) + npm run i18n:check

zones.title: Workspace UI and shared primitives — two themes from one codebase

constraints.rule: Never hardcode a color outside app/landing/.
constraints.why: A literal hex cannot follow [data-theme="dark"], so every one is a surface that silently stops theming. Use brand tokens (ink, paper, steel, coral, moss, limewash, dial-*, score-*), then the theme-remapped neutrals and mapped status shades; add the dark value when introducing a new shade.
constraints.enforced_by: eslint no-restricted-syntax (hex / rgba selectors, error) + npm run design:check

constraints.rule: Compose recurring surfaces from app/_components/ui/recipes.ts (PANEL, CHIP, BTN_*, EYEBROW, FIELD).
constraints.why: Re-typing a Tailwind class string is how two surfaces drift apart between themes. Write once, apply many.

constraints.rule: Express a theme difference at the cheapest layer that holds it.
constraints.why: token -> a `dark:` variant in a recipe (it follows data-theme, not the OS) -> a markup fork via `hidden dark:contents` / `contents dark:hidden` -> a behavioral fork via useTheme(). Never a JS fork where CSS suffices. There is no `.theme-light-only` / `.theme-dark-only` utility pair — an earlier revision of the canonical file named one that does not exist.

constraints.rule: No VALUE import of a db store; `import type` only.
constraints.why: These modules reach data through a route handler. A store imported here compiles better-sqlite3 into a component graph. The value imports belong in a server component under app/<route>/page.tsx.

constraints.rule: Verify a new surface in BOTH themes before finishing.
constraints.why: The themes differ in structure, not only color (Spark Dark adds drawn outlines, sticker shadows, tilt, a display face, spring easing). The appearance control is on the sidebar rail.

zones.title: The workspace shell — one place that knows the tab ids

constraints.rule: Tab ids live ONCE, in app/features/shell/tabs.ts.
constraints.why: The workspace is a single page driven by `?tab=`. A second list of ids is a second source of truth for what the app contains.
constraints.enforced_by: prose (the literal-array + derived-union + runtime-guard pattern makes a stray id a tsc error at the use site)

constraints.rule: Closed vocabularies use literal-array + derived union + runtime guard.
constraints.why: It is the recurring pattern here (tabs.ts, i18n/locales.ts): one array is the vocabulary, the union type is derived from it, and the guard validates untrusted input against the same array — so adding a member is one edit and forgetting a case is a compile error.

constraints.rule: This directory is a FIXED art direction and is the only place raw hex is legal.
constraints.why: It is the Spark landing art, not a themed product surface. That exemption stops at this directory — do not cite it anywhere else.
constraints.enforced_by: eslint (the design block ignores this glob)

constraints.rule: It is still fully localized and held at ERROR for hardcoded strings.
constraints.why: These components serve /, /about and /market in production in four languages. The old carve-out was retiring 50 strings' worth of debt by ignoring it.

zones.title: Message catalogs — four locales, one change

constraints.rule: Every key added to messages/en.json lands in cs, de and fr in the SAME change.
constraints.why: next-intl keys are typed: a t("missing.key") is a tsc error, so an incomplete catalog breaks `npm run typecheck` for everyone, not just the locale you skipped. en is the source of truth.

constraints.rule: Server-written text stores a catalog reference, not a rendered string.
constraints.why: A row written server-side has no reader locale. Task labels store a reference (app/_lib/task-label.ts) resolved at render time; a lint on JSX text could never catch those.

zones.title: The LLM chokepoint — degrading keyless is a product property

constraints.rule: Never make a provider mandatory, and never remove a deterministic fallback.
constraints.why: Keyless degradation is a product property, not a dev convenience — a fresh install with no API key must work. It is certified by the automation_eval and fault_eval gates, and it is on record as an ADR.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run test:eval:ci (matching_eval, automation_eval --no-llm, fault_eval — all strict, keyless, in ci.yml python-gate)

constraints.rule: Keep app/_lib/llm-config.ts and pipeline/jobfit/llm/capabilities.py in step.
constraints.why: They are the two halves of one multi-provider registry; a provider added to one and not the other is a route that works in TypeScript and dies in Python.

constraints.rule: Tests are MANDATORY for changes here.
constraints.why: Auth, billing, tenancy, rate limits and this chokepoint are the five areas where a test is not optional.

zones.title: pipeline/jobfit — spawned per request, schema-coupled to TypeScript

constraints.rule: Schemas are generated, not hand-mirrored: run `npm run schemas:gen` (it is what `typecheck` and `build` run first).
constraints.why: pipeline/jobfit/codegen is the single source for the TS/Python schema pair. Editing the generated TS by hand is undone by the next build.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run typecheck / npm run build (schemas:gen runs first); npm run schemas:check

constraints.rule: New ruff suppressions need a declared ceiling.
constraints.why: ruff.toml is a ratchet: each ignored rule is documented debt with a `# ratchet: <CODE> <= <N>` ceiling, and `ruff check` alone can never report that its own exceptions are multiplying. autofix.yml lowers the ceilings on every PR.

constraints.rule: A new skipped test raises the gate's baseline deliberately.
constraints.why: run_gated.py fails when skips exceed KP_SKIP_BASELINE (5, with a per-skip derivation written in ci.yml) so a critical test cannot silently stop running.

constraints.rule: The pipeline is spawned per request on purpose — do not convert it to a service without reading the decision record.
constraints.why: That, the pinned Next canary, the single SQLite file and the deterministic fallbacks are written decisions in docs/architecture/decisions/, each ending with the observation that would reopen it.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run docs:check (ADR sources must resolve)

zones.title: packages/ — the lane that must stay liftable

constraints.rule: A package never imports from app/ — not even `import type`.
constraints.why: packages/voice-tts is built to be lifted out of this repo intact, with its providers behind /api/tts and swapped by env. The dependency only ever points app/ -> packages/. A type import breaks source portability even though it is free at runtime.

constraints.rule: Package tests run in the same unit suite.
constraints.why: `npm run test:unit` globs packages/**/*.test.ts alongside app/**/*.test.ts.

zones.title: Workflows and the scripts that judge changes

constraints.rule: Nothing an outsider can influence may be interpolated into a `run:` or a `script:`.
constraints.why: `${{ }}` is substituted into the script TEXT before the interpreter starts, so an issue title in a `run:` line is that title as code. Pass it through `env:` on the step and read "$VAR". This repository dispatches agents from issues and publishes signed images, so the distance from a stranger's text to the supply chain is one such line.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run security:actions (rules run-injection / script-injection / untrusted-checkout / no-permissions, blocking, in ci.yml node-quality)

constraints.rule: A new action is pinned to a full commit SHA with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z`.
constraints.why: A tag is a pointer its owner can move. The floating refs that remain are enumerated in .github/actions-pin-allowlist.json as debt that can only shrink — do not add an entry to make a red build green.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run security:actions (rule `unpinned`, blocking); pin-actions.yml resolves the allowlisted ones weekly

constraints.rule: A required check is named in .github/rulesets/main.json by its job `name:`.
constraints.why: Renaming a job without renaming it there silently un-gates it: GitHub waits forever for a check nothing reports.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run review:gate (offline half, in ci.yml node-quality)

constraints.rule: An agent dispatched from an issue may never write to the machinery that judges it.
constraints.why: scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs refuses .github/workflows, .github/rulesets, .githooks, .claude/ and scripts/{review,security,hooks,docs,lint,agent}. There is no override flag, and a fixture asserts every lens, hook and workflow in the tree is still inside a protected prefix.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run test:agent (blocking, in ci.yml node-quality)

constraints.rule: A new job in ci.yml needs a ceiling in ci-budget.json, strictly below its own timeout-minutes.
constraints.why: `timeout-minutes` is a crash barrier, not a budget: a job drifting from 6 to 18 minutes passes every gate while halving throughput. A ceiling at or above the timeout could never fire first, which makes it decoration.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run test:perf (offline coupling check) + the Pipeline budget job (measures the real run)

zones.title: Playwright — the keyless subset is a decision, not a glob

constraints.rule: Specs in the CI subset are named ONE BY ONE in ci.yml, never by a shared prefix.
constraints.why: That job is the release gate. A filter that widens as files are added is how a slow or key-needing spec ends up in the keyless subset without anyone deciding to put it there. Adding a spec there IS the decision.
constraints.enforced_by: prose (the explicit list in ci.yml e2e-deterministic)

constraints.rule: A spec in that subset must be keyless by construction, and its header says which endpoint on its path degrades deterministically.
constraints.why: The run certifies the degraded-gracefully product property; a spec that quietly needs a provider turns a product guarantee into a flake.

zones.title: docs/ — the doc changes with the behavior

constraints.rule: When you change behavior, update the doc that describes it in the SAME change.
constraints.why: scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json maps source globs to the doc that documents them. A feature doc naming a moved file or a renamed stage is worse than no doc — that drift is why this tree was reorganized.
constraints.enforced_by: the Stop hook (check-doc-sync.mjs) locally + the doc-sync CI job over the git range; waive on the record with a `Doc-sync: internal-only — <why>` commit trailer

constraints.rule: A new feature area adds its entry to feature-doc-map.json in the same change.
constraints.why: Otherwise nothing watches it.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run test:docs (the fixtures validate that every mapped doc exists and every glob root resolves)

constraints.rule: Anything future-looking goes in docs/concepts/ or docs/BACKLOG.md, never in a feature doc.
constraints.why: A feature doc states what is implemented TODAY. docs/_archive/ is superseded material and is not current.

zones.title: Everything — the rules with no scope

constraints.rule: Stage with pathspecs: `git add <path> <path>`, never -A / . / -u.
constraints.why: Multiple agent sessions work in this checkout concurrently on disjoint files. Before committing, check `git diff --cached --stat` — if the staged count exceeds what you added, `git restore --staged` the strangers first. Never `git stash` or discard work that is not yours.

constraints.rule: Conventional commit subjects: `type(scope): summary`.
constraints.why: scripts/release/prepare.mjs cuts every CHANGELOG section from these prefixes, so a subject without one vanishes from the release note an operator upgrades on. The subject is ONE clause — no session report, no first person; the body has no length limit.
constraints.enforced_by: .githooks/commit-msg locally + the commit-convention CI job over the range; waive with a `Commit-convention-exemption: <why>` trailer

constraints.rule: Verify with `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`.
constraints.why: These three are the declared verify set in .ai/manifest.yaml, and every guidance file must name them identically — that list exists because renaming a script once left a projection telling agents to run the old one with every per-file check still green.
constraints.enforced_by: npm run guidance:check (blocking, in ci.yml node-quality)

$comment: Which parts of the tree have WRITTEN constraints, and which are ASSUMED —
i.e. covered only by the global document. This is the answer to 'was this
context's guidance ever written, or merely assumed', and it is deliberately
stated rather than computed, because a computed number would go green the
moment someone added an empty stanza.
To re-derive it: for each context in context-map.json, test its `file_paths`
against every zone's `paths`. A context matched only by `repo-wide` is
assumed, not written.

assumed.note: Covered by `ui-surfaces` for theming, i18n and the db rule, but their own domain invariants (what an analytics funnel may recompute, which tool results are cacheable) are not written down anywhere yet.

Operator/dev-facing surfaces with deliberately different rules from the product UI (the inspector is a FIXED devtools skin that must not follow the app theme). Stated in eslint's ignores, not as guidance.

assumed.area: app/_lib/** outside db/ and the llm files
assumed.note: The largest assumed area: ~100 domain modules (comms, schedule, decisions, devcase, matching) whose constraints live in their feature docs under docs/features/<area>/ but are not attached to a scope here.
Data and ops scripts (market pulse, db dump/load, seeding). No stated constraints beyond repo-wide.
